result.title: Polytropos: What Do Vision-Language Model Descriptions Make of a Cultural Object?
result.summary: Vision-language models have become a new kind of describer, writing about almost anything people see, and their descriptions now shape how cultures are known by people and by other models. Descriptions of cultures tend to turn particular things into types, and what a description loses shows what its describer lacks. We introduce Polytropos, a benchmark that measures what model descriptions of cultural objects keep of the particular object by turning each description back into an image and comparing it with the original photograph. On 374 objects from the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Getty, with 1,870 descriptions from five models and 230 written by curators, reconstructions are recognised as the recorded culture more often than the photographs, at 54.55% to 59.09% against 52.14%, yet 16% to 21% of objects change outcome and only 0.49% of reconstructions are identified as the specific object. On the same objects, models lose recorded cultures at a rate similar to curators but gain more. Model descriptions give each object many faces, each typical of its culture and almost none the object itself.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 Polytropos 基准：将五个模型与策展人对 374 件博物馆藏品写的描述重新生成图像并与原照片比较，测量描述保留了多少对象特殊性，发现重建更像「该文化」而非该具体物件。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接诊断 VLM 描述中对象级视觉细节的流失与「典型化」偏差，与视觉细节保留、信息坍缩问题相关；其「描述→重建→比对」探针可能可供核查 latent 状态中任务必要信息保留程度的评测设计。
